title: Introduction to the BetaDanish Package
text: BetaDanish package provides comprehensive suite tools survival reliability analysis using Beta-Danish distribution. Classical lifetime models, Weibull, Gamma, Log-Normal distributions, often limited hazard shape flexibility. typically force hazard rate strictly monotonic , best, unimodal. Beta-Danish distribution overcomes limitations accommodating decreasing, increasing, unimodal (upside-bathtub), bathtub-shaped hazard rates within single, unified four-parameter family. package implements core mathematical functions, robust Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) complete right-censored data, advanced modules Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) regression, cure-rate models, competing risks.

title: Introduction to the BetaDanish Package
text: many clinical datasets (like transplant data), proportion patients may “cured” never experience event. Standard survival models force survival curve zero, misrepresents data. BetaDanish package provides fit_bd_cure() function fit Mixture Promotion-Time (Non-Mixture) cure models.

title: Competing Risks with the Beta-Danish Distribution
text: independent latent failure times, joint competing-risks likelihood factorises one Beta-Danish marginal per cause. vignette demonstrates fitting diagnostic plotting. cmprsk installed, code chunks skipped.

title: Competing Risks with the Beta-Danish Distribution
code: library(BetaDanish) set.seed(2026) n  <- 400 T1 <- rbetadanish(n, a = 1.2, b = 1.5, c = 1.0, k = 0.4) T2 <- rbetadanish(n, a = 1.0, b = 2.0, c = 1.0, k = 0.2) C  <- stats::rexp(n, 0.05) time  <- pmin(T1, T2, C) cause <- ifelse(time == C, 0L, ifelse(T1 <= T2, 1L, 2L)) table(cause) #> cause #>   0   1   2  #>  23 198 179

title: Cure Models with the Beta-Danish Distribution
text: package implements two cure formulations Exponentiated Danish kernel: Mixture cure splits population susceptible fraction pi(Z) modelled logistic regression incidence covariates, cured fraction 1 - pi(Z). Promotion-time cure derives cure fraction latent Poisson process clonogenic cells intensity theta(Z) = exp(Z' gamma); cure fraction exp(-theta(Z)). fitted via fit_bd_cure().

title: Cure Models with the Beta-Danish Distribution
text: fits use simulated data known cure structure.
code: library(BetaDanish) set.seed(2026) n <- 250 z <- stats::rbinom(n, 1, 0.5) pi_susc <- stats::plogis(0.3 + 0.7 * z) cured   <- stats::rbinom(n, 1, 1 - pi_susc) == 1 T_true  <- ifelse(cured, Inf,                   rbetadanish(n, a = 1, b = 2, c = 1.5, k = 0.4)) C   <- stats::rexp(n, 0.04) time   <- pmin(T_true, C) status <- ifelse(T_true <= C, 1, 0) dat <- data.frame(time = time, status = status, z = z) cat("Sample size:", n, " Censoring rate:", round(mean(status == 0), 2), "\n") #> Sample size: 250  Censoring rate: 0.45

title: BetaDanish
text: Core distribution: numerically stable d/p/q/r/h/s/logS Beta-Danish Danish baseline. MLE inference: complete right-censored data delta-method standard errors multi-start optimization. Bayesian inference: bayes_betadanish() random-walk Metropolis sampler (requires MCMCpack). AFT regression mixture / promotion-time cure models. Competing risks: bound-constrained multi-start L-BFGS-B Aalen-Johansen overlay Gray’s test (cif_compare()). Structural properties: moments existence checks, probability-weighted moments, mean residual life, Shannon entropy, order statistics, stress-strength reliability, hazard-shape classifier. Diagnostics: survival, hazard, density, P-P, Q-Q, Cox-Snell residual plots. Tooling: bootstrap confidence intervals finite-sample simulation-study runner.
